# #2520 yq: alias sync, anchor marks and the alias redirect apply only to the last document of a multi-document stream

**Severity: Medium** — silent wrong values and dropped anchors in every document but the last of a stream.

## Summary

In a multi-document YAML stream, alias value sync (#711), anchor/alias mark preservation (#763) and the #1351 alias redirect apply only to the **last** document. Every earlier document is written positionally with its `&x`/`*x` marks dropped. Found by the review of PR #2510; reproduces on `main` (`a353c85ba`) before that PR, so it is pre-existing.

## Repro

Verified against Homebrew `yq` v4.53.3:

```console
$ printf 'a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x\n---\na: &x {p: 3}\nb: *x\n' | yq '.b.p = 9'
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x
---
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x

$ printf 'a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x\n---\na: &x {p: 3}\nb: *x\n' | succinctly yq '.a.p = 9'   # main
a: {p: 9}
b:
  p: 1
---
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x
```

Document 0 loses `&x`/`*x` and `b` does not follow the anchor write; document 1 is right. With three documents only the third is right; `--doc 0` reproduces on its own.

## Root cause (not isolated)

Something in the per-document path of `evaluate_yaml_cursor` — `cursor.index().has_aliases()`, `collect_alias_groups(cursor)`, or the comment-tree capture — answers for the whole stream or for the final document rather than the document at hand. `has_aliases()` being an index-wide flag while `collect_alias_groups` walks the per-document cursor is the first thing to check.

## Suggested fix direction

Make the alias-sensitivity gate and the group collection per document (or per document cursor), then add multi-document twins of the existing `#711`/`#763`/`#1351` CLI tests, including `--doc 0`.

## Why this is separate from #1351

#1351 (PR #2510) changes what a write does inside one document; this is about which documents of a stream get that treatment at all, and it predates the PR.


---

## Comments on this issue


**Comment by newhoggy:**

## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** **no longer reproduces.** The issue's own repro now matches Homebrew yq v4.53.3 byte-for-byte:

```console
$ printf 'a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x\n---\na: &x {p: 3}\nb: *x\n' | succinctly yq '.a.p = 9'
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x
---
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x
```

Also identical to yq (diffed, all 12 cells): `.b.p = 9`, `.a.p |= . + 1`, `del(.a.p)`, `.c += [2]` on three further streams — a stream where only document 0 has an alias, one where only document 1 does, and one with different anchor names per document (`&x`/`&z`/`&w`). Three-document stream: all three documents get the redirect and keep their marks. `--doc 0` on the two-doc stream prints `a: &x {p: 9}` / `b: *x`. `-i '.b.p = 9'` on a scratch copy writes both documents with marks intact, same bytes as `yq -i`. The one route still positional is `--eval-all` (`succinctly yq --eval-all '.b.p = 9'` writes `b: {p: 9}` and drops both marks in *every* document), which `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` already records as a separate, known gap — not this issue.

**Root cause / mechanism:** the report predates the #1351/#2497 series landing (`e001e31b5` … `4e4cf633e`, `7777a0175`, `881af42b8`, `a8f8e7b6d`) and #2072's cursor node-id change (`ae5cd88f4`). On current `main`, `evaluate_yaml_direct_filtered` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) hands each document's own `YamlCursor` (from `docs.uncons_cursor()`) to `evaluate_yaml_cursor`, which snapshots `alias_sync_ctx` via `collect_alias_groups(cursor)` (a per-document walk) and installs the `alias_identity` table from those groups around `eval_with_cursor_using`, per call. `cursor.index().has_aliases()` is still index-wide, but it is only a "could this matter" gate — with a stream where only document 1 has aliases, document 0 collects an empty group set and is written positionally, which is correct. I could not build the pre-fix commit under the triage rules (read-only tree), so the exact fixing commit is not attributed; the whole series is between the issue's `a353c85ba` and `HEAD`.

**Plan:**
1. Pin it. Add multi-document twins of the existing #711/#763/#1351 CLI tests to `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`: the two-doc repro (`.a.p = 9` and `.b.p = 9`), a three-doc stream, the two mixed streams above (alias in doc 0 only / doc 1 only), the different-anchor-names stream, `--doc 0` and `--doc 1`, and `-i` on a scratch copy asserting the exact bytes. Capture every expected output from yq v4.53.3 in the test's doc comment, per the existing convention in that file.
2. Optional attribution: `git bisect run` between `a353c85ba` and `HEAD` with a release build and the two-doc repro, and name the commit in the closing comment — nice to have, not required to close.
3. Docs: delete the sentence "A multi-document stream applies the redirect and the anchor marks to the last document only ([#2520], pre-existing)." from the `#1351` section of `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`; keep the `--eval-all` sentence just before it, which is still true.
4. Close as fixed once the tests are on `main`.

**Risks / open questions:** none of substance — the only risk is closing without a test and having the per-document snapshot regress silently later, which step 1 covers. If the bisect attributes the fix to something incidental (e.g. the node-id change), say so in the test's doc comment so the pin is understood as load-bearing.

**Dependencies / related:** #1351 / PR #2510 (the redirect), #2497 (mark propagation), #711, #763; `--eval-all` gap is recorded separately in `limitations.md` and would need its own issue if anyone wants it. No open PR references #2520.

**Class:** Sonnet — the behaviour is already correct on `main`; what remains is adding oracle-pinned CLI tests to one file, removing one stale sentence from `limitations.md`, and closing. No judgment calls, no evaluator changes.

# #2588 yq: =`'s right side still yields false for a zero-node literal/constructor operand (#2540 residual)

## Summary

[#2540](https://github.com/rust-works/succinctly/issues/2540) fixed `and`/`or`'s own read-only-context handling of a literal/constructor operand whose upstream pipe stage produced zero nodes (e.g. `(.a.zz | true) and true` now correctly answers `true`, matching real yq). The identical `Context.DontAutoCreate` mechanism (#2470) also applies to `=`'s right side, and it diverges the same way:

```console
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nx: 5\n' | yq -o=json -I0 '.x = (.a.zz | true)'
{"a":{"b":1},"x":true}
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nx: 5\n' | succinctly yq -o=json -I0 '.x = (.a.zz | true)'
{"a":{"b":1},"x":5}
```

Real yq gives `x: true`; succinctly leaves `x` unchanged (`5`).

## Why #2540 didn't cover this

`and`/`or` evaluate their operands through `jq::eval::boolean_fanout_bools`, shared by both evaluators, which is where #2540's fix (`yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor`) was added. `=`'s right side evaluates through a completely separate mechanism (`jq::eval::yq_prepare_assign_targets`/`resolve_dynamic_indexes`), which #2540 did not touch — fixing this needs its own trace through that code path, not a second call to the same classifier from the wrong place.

## Suggested approach

Find wherever `=`'s right side currently registers "zero outputs" for the empty-context case (likely near `yq_prepare_assign_targets`'s own handling of a read-only right-side evaluation, #2470/#2481) and consult `jq::eval::yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor` there the same way `boolean_fanout_bools` now does, before falling through to the existing "target unchanged" behavior.

## Verification notes

Re-verify the same shape matrix #2540 already established (literal, `[...]` — regardless of body, `{...}` — only when every field value also independently qualifies) against `=`'s right side specifically, since the surrounding mechanism differs even though the underlying "is this operand really empty" classification should be identical.

## Related

- #2540 (fixed `and`/`or`'s own copy of this gap)
- #2470 (the read-only context mechanism both share)
- `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`'s "An `and`/`or` operand's evaluation context" section, which already documents this residual


---

## Comments on this issue


**Comment by newhoggy:**

## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** still reproduces, and the residual is wider than "literal/constructor on `=`'s right side" — #2540's classifier is *itself* too narrow, and that shows on `and`/`or` too. Re-probed live against Homebrew yq v4.53.3 on `a: {b: 1}` / `x: 5` (`-o=json -I0`; `.a.zz` genuinely absent):

| filter                                   | yq v4.53.3        | succinctly yq       |
|------------------------------------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| `.x = (.a.zz \| true)` / `7` / `"s"` / `null` / `-1` | that value | `x: 5` (unchanged) |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| [1,2])`, `[.b]`, `[true]`, `[]` | `x: []`     | unchanged           |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| {"q": 1})`               | `x: {"q":1}`      | unchanged           |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| {"q": [1]})`             | `x: {"q":[]}`     | unchanged           |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| {"q": .b})`, `.b`, `length`, `tostring`, `. // 3`, `select(true)` | unchanged | unchanged (agree) |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| 1 + 1)`, `"s" + "t"`, `1 == 1`, `1 // 3` | `2`, `"st"`, `true`, `1` | unchanged |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| true \| not)`, `1 \| tostring`, `[1] \| length`, `{"q": 1} \| .q`, `"a" \| test("a")`, `1 \| . + 1` | `false`, `"1"`, `0`, `1`, `true`, `2` | unchanged |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| (true, false))`, `(1, .b)`, `(.b, 1)` | `false`, `1`, `1` | unchanged |
| `.x = ([.a.zz \| true])`                 | `x: [true]`       | `x: []`             |
| `.x \|= (.zz \| true)`                   | `x: true`         | unchanged           |
| `.x += (.a.zz \| 1)`                     | `x: 6`            | unchanged           |
| `.zz = (.a.zz \| true)`                  | `zz: true`        | `zz: null`          |
| `(.x, .a.b) = (.a.zz \| true)`           | both `true`       | unchanged           |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| 1) + 1`, `((.a.zz \| 1) == 1)`, `((.a.zz \| 1) // 3)` | `2`, `true`, `1` | `1`, `false`, `3` |
| `(.a.zz \| 1 + 1) and true`              | `true`            | **`false`**         |
| `(.a.zz \| false \| not) and true`, `(.a.zz \| [1] \| length) and true` | `true` | **`false`** |
| `(.a.zz \| (true, false)) and true`      | `true`, `false` (two results) | **`false`** (one) |
| `(.a.zz \| 1) + 1` (top level, read-only) | `2`              | `1`                 |

Agreeing rows: `.x = (.a[5] | true)` (`true` in both — an out-of-range index does not go empty), `.x = (.a.zz | true | . and false)` (`false`), `.x = (.a.zz | true and false)` (`false`), `.x = (1,2)` (`2`, yq's collapse-to-last). Note `{q: 1}`, `empty` and `if` are lexer errors in real yq, so they are not oracle cells.

**Root cause / mechanism:** two layers.

1. The consumer gap the issue names: `collect_rhs_outputs` (`src/jq/eval.rs`, the prologue shared by `eval_assign`/`eval_compound_assign`/`eval_alternative_assign`) enters `yq_read_only_context` (#2470) and, when the right side yields `QueryResult::None`, returns an empty vector that `normalize_rhs_values_for_fork` turns into "one document, target auto-created, never written". It never consults `yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor` the way `empty_boolean_operand_bit` does. The generic evaluator's owned-identity pipe (`eval_generic.rs`, the `needs_path_context(stage)` branch that builds `yq_assign_rhs_document`) prefetches through the same function, so it inherits the fix.
2. The classifier gap: `yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor` models yq's rule as "the pipe's *last* stage re-emits a static value". Real yq's model (verified from `operator_value.go`/`operator_collect.go`/`operator_create_map.go` for #2540) is per-operator: the *first* context-free stage re-emits its node(s) into an otherwise-empty context, and every later stage then runs normally on those nodes. That is why `true | not`, `[1] | length`, `1 + 1` (both operands re-emit, then add), `(true, false)` (both branches re-emit), and `(.a.zz | 1) + 1` (the operand pipe re-emits `1`) all produce values in yq. The same classifier feeds `and`/`or`, so those rows are wrong today too.

**Plan:**
1. Replace `yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor(expr) -> Option<OwnedValue>` with `yq_empty_context_reemit(expr) -> Option<Expr>` in `src/jq/eval.rs`: return an expression that, evaluated against a `null` input inside the read-only scope, reproduces what yq emits. Rules: `Literal` → itself; `Array(_)` → the literal `[]` (regardless of body); `Object` → itself only if every key and value is itself re-emittable with no pipe remainder (keep #2540's all-or-nothing rule; `{"q": [1]}` → `{"q": []}`, so rewrite the field values too); `Comma` → the comma of the re-emittable branches, `None` if none qualify (`(1, .b)` → `1`); `Neg` → itself if its operand qualifies; `Arithmetic`/`Compare`/`And`/`Or`/`Alternative` → itself if both operands qualify (evaluated against `null`, a context-free operand tree gives the same answer as yq's re-emit); `Pipe(stages)` → find the first stage `i` that qualifies, return `Pipe([rewritten_i, stages[i+1..]...])` — the remainder runs on the seed values through the ordinary evaluator; `Paren` via `strip_parens` as today. Anything else → `None`.
2. `collect_rhs_outputs`: in the `QueryResult::None` arm (and `Partial(vs, _)` with empty `vs` only if the control is not an error — check `Break`/`Halt` ordering against #400/#494 first), consult `yq_empty_context_reemit(value_expr)` under `S::READ_ONLY_ABSENT_KEY_IS_EMPTY`; if `Some(rewritten)`, evaluate it with `eval_owned_input::<W, S>(&rewritten, &OwnedValue::Null, optional)` *inside the still-open `_scope`* and return those outputs. The existing `normalize_rhs_values_for_fork` then applies yq's collapse-to-last, which gives `(true, false)` → `false` and `(.x, .a.b) = …` its fan-out for free.
3. `empty_boolean_operand_bit` (`eval.rs`) and its twin `read_only_operand_strategy_generic` (`eval_generic.rs`): evaluate the rewritten expression instead of taking one static value, and push *every* output's truthiness bit — `(.a.zz | (true, false)) and true` must yield two results. `boolean_fanout_bools` is already the shared entry point, so wire the rewrite there once.
4. Arithmetic/comparison/alternative operands in read-only context (`eval_binary_fanout`'s empty-operand path, `empty_outer_operand_pass` and `empty_outer_operand_pass_generic`): before falling to `yq_empty_operand_output` (#2460), consult the rewrite for the empty operand — this closes `(.a.zz | 1) + 1` and `((.a.zz | 1) // 3)`. Gate on `rules.read_only` exactly like step 3; jq mode and non-read-only yq contexts are untouched (`(.a.zz | 1) + 1` at the top level already agrees because `.a.zz` auto-creates there).
5. Tests: rename/extend `test_yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor_and_operand_2540` and `test_yq_empty_context_constructor_value_shapes_2540` in `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs` with every row of the table above for `=`, `|=`, `+=`, `and`/`or`, and the arithmetic-operand rows; keep the agreeing rows as negative controls (`{"q": .b}`, `.b`, `length`, `select(true)`, `.a[5]`). Unit tests for `yq_empty_context_reemit` in `src/jq/eval.rs` (pipe with a qualifying head and a non-qualifying tail, comma with mixed branches, object with a nested array field). A jq-mode guard row (`/usr/bin/jq '.x = (.a.zz | true)'` on the JSON twin gives `x: true` because jq's `.a.zz` is `null`, not empty — so jq mode must not enter this path at all).
6. Docs: rewrite `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`'s "An `and`/`or` operand's evaluation context — resolved for `and`/`or` (#2540); `=`'s right side remains open" section: drop the "Residual, not yet fixed" paragraph, replace the "last stage" description with the first-context-free-stage model, and extend the captured matrix with the new rows. Update `yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor`'s doc comment (it documents the old model in detail).

**Risks / open questions:**
- The classifier is shared by `and`/`or`: widening it changes those answers too (correctly per the table, but it is a second behaviour change in one PR — call both out and pin both).
- Evaluating the rewritten expression against `null` is only sound because every stage kept in it is context-free by construction; a stage the classifier admits by mistake (`Expr::Shared` is deliberately not unwrapped today — keep it that way) would read `null` where yq reads nothing. Keep the admitted set closed and enumerate it in the doc comment.
- `Partial` with a trailing control: decide whether a `Break`/`Halt` after zero outputs still gets the re-emit (probe `.x = (.a.zz | 1, halt)`-style shapes only if yq's lexer accepts them; it rejects `empty`, so the space is small).
- Multi-target `(.x, .a.b) = …` goes through the same prologue; confirm the fork loop sees the seeded values once, not once per target.

**Dependencies / related:** #2540 (the classifier being generalised), #2470 (read-only scope), #2481 (`yq_assign_rhs_document`), #2460 (`yq_empty_operand_output`, which stays the fallback). No open PR references #2588.

**Class:** Opus — the fix is not "call the existing classifier from one more place": the classifier's model is wrong and has to be re-derived from a matrix into a rewrite-and-continue form, then wired into four consumers across both evaluators (`=` family, `and`/`or`, arithmetic/comparison operands, and the generic owned-identity prefetch). The oracle pins every cell, so no ADR or new representation is needed (not Fable), but the change reaches shared operand-emptiness machinery with real regression risk for the #2460/#2540 rows that already agree.

# #2598 yq: a mapping key's anchor is still dropped on the DOM write path (=, |=, del(), -P, --arg)

## Background

#1352 fixed `write_yaml_field_key` (`src/yaml/light.rs`) to emit a mapping
key's own `&anchor`, matching real yq -- but that fix only covers the
cursor-streaming identity path (`YamlCursor::stream_yaml_value`, reached by
a plain `.`/no-op query and `--sort-keys`).

## Remaining bug

The DOM emitter -- reached by a write (`=`, `|=`, `del()`, ...) or a
DOM-forcing flag (`-P`, `--arg`, `-o=json` for JSON output specifically) --
still drops a mapping key's anchor. Confirmed live against yq v4.53.3:

```console
$ printf '&k key: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq '.b = 5'
key: 1
b: 5
$ printf '&k key: 1\nb: 2\n' | yq '.b = 5'
&k key: 1
b: 5
```

(`-o=json` output is correct in both -- JSON has no anchors to lose.)

## Root cause

`yaml_quote_key` in `src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs` takes only the key
string; nothing in the DOM write path threads a key's anchor mark through
`CommentTree` the way #763 did for *value* anchors (`NodeMeta::anchor` on
`CommentTree::Leaf`/`Array`/`Object`'s own metadata).

## Suggested fix direction

`CommentTree::Object`'s existing key-scoped map (`IndexMap<String, (String,
bool)>`, #765's per-key deferred-value comment slot) is the natural place
for a key anchor mark to join, per #1352's own suggested fix direction --
rather than a fourth parallel structure. This needs threading through:
- the builder (`to_owned_with_comments`/`to_owned_with_comments_at_depth`,
  capturing `field.key_cursor().anchor()` per field)
- `reconcile_presentation_at_depth` (keeping a field's key anchor when the
  write didn't touch that field)
- the DOM emitter (`emit_yaml_value`/`yaml_quote_key` in `yq_runner.rs`)
- likely `enforce_anchor_soundness` too, if a key anchor can itself be an
  alias target elsewhere in the document (unconfirmed -- worth checking
  whether real yq even permits aliasing to a key-anchored node's value this
  way before assuming symmetry with #763's soundness handling).

Larger and riskier than #1352's own scope (which is why it wasn't attempted
there), similar in shape to #763's own original build-out.


---

## Comments on this issue


**Comment by newhoggy:**

## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** still reproduces exactly as filed, and the matrix is wider than the body's one row. Against Homebrew yq v4.53.3 (identity `.` agrees in every case — #1352's streaming fix holds):

| input                              | filter                      | yq v4.53.3                            | succinctly yq                      |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `&k key: 1` / `b: 2`               | `.b = 5`                    | `&k key: 1` / `b: 5`                  | `key: 1` / `b: 5`                  |
| same                               | `.key \|= . + 1`, `del(.b)`, `.a.b = 7`, `.key = 9`, `-P '.'` | keeps `&k`  | drops `&k`                         |
| `&k key: 1` / `b: *k`              | `.b = 5`                    | `&k key: 1` / `b: 5`                  | `key: 1` / `b: 5`                  |
| same                               | `.key \|= . + 1`            | `&k key: 2` / `b: *k`                 | `key: 2` / **`b: key`**            |
| same                               | `.a.b = 7`, `.key = 9`      | `&k …` / `b: *k`                      | `key …` / **`b: key`**             |
| `a:` / `  &k key: 1` / `  b: 2` / `c: *k` | `.b = 5`, `del(.b)`, `.a.b = 7` | `&k key` kept, `c: *k` kept | `key` bare, **`c: key`**           |
| `{&k key: 1, b: 2}`                | `.b = 5`                    | `{&k key: 1, b: 5}`                   | `{key: 1, b: 5}`                   |
| `&k key: # kc` / `  x: 1` / `b: 2` | `.b = 5`                    | `&k key: # kc` / `  x: 1` / `b: 5`    | `key: # kc` …                      |
| `? &k key` / `: 1` / `b: 2`        | `.b = 5`                    | `&k key: 1` / `b: 5`                  | `key: 1` / `b: 5`                  |
| `&k 1: x` / `b: 2`                 | `.b = 5`                    | `&k 1: x` / `b: 5`                    | `1: x` / `b: 5`                    |

The bold cells are the second-order damage: a value alias that targets a *key's* anchor (`b: *k`, value `"key"`) is expanded to `b: key` on every DOM write, because `enforce_anchor_soundness` never sees a `&k` declaration and drops the `*k` mark. `-o json` is identical in both (no anchors in JSON). `.key | key | anchor` already answers `k` in both, so the *read* side has the key's anchor; only the DOM write/emit route loses it.

**Root cause / mechanism:** `to_owned_with_comments_at_depth` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) captures per-field metadata only from `field.value_cursor` (`own_anchor` via `DocumentCursor::alias/anchor`) and from `field.key_cursor.line_comment_raw()` into `CommentTree::Object`'s third slot (`IndexMap<String, (String, bool)>`, #765). Nothing captures `field.key_cursor.anchor()`. Downstream, `emit_yaml_value_at_depth` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) builds each key with `yaml_quote_key(k)` in both its flow-mapping and block-mapping arms and prefixes an anchor only from the *value's* `anchor_decl_prefix(field_comments)`; `reconcile_presentation_at_depth` copies only the `(comment, absent)` pair per key; `strip_presentation_style_at_depth` clones the key map as-is; and `scan_anchor_soundness` records `declared` anchors from node metas only, so a key-anchored `*k` is "unresolvable". The streaming twin, `write_yaml_field_key` (`src/yaml/light.rs`, #1352), already does the right thing — it is the model for the emitter.

**Plan:**
1. Widen the key slot rather than add a fourth parallel map: in `src/jq/eval_generic.rs` replace `CommentTree::Object`'s `IndexMap<String, (String, bool)>` with `IndexMap<String, KeyMeta>` where `KeyMeta { comment: Option<(String, bool)>, anchor: Option<String> }` (a key can only *declare*; an alias-as-key `*k : 2` is a separate, pre-existing gap — see risks). Keep `key_comment`/`key_comment_if_value_absent` as accessors and add `key_anchor(&self, key) -> Option<&str>`. Update all nine `CommentTree::Object(` construction sites (`git grep -n "CommentTree::Object("` across `src/jq/eval_generic.rs`, `src/jq/eval.rs`, `src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`).
2. Builder: in `to_owned_with_comments_at_depth`, capture `field.key_cursor.anchor()` per field (through the `DocumentCursor` trait method so the JSON impl stays a `None` default), applying the same #2500 `under_alias` suppression the value `Declares` mark gets — a key anchor seen inside an alias-expanded subtree is the target's own mark, not a second declaration.
3. Reconcile: in `reconcile_presentation_at_depth`'s object arm, carry the pristine key's anchor alongside its comment under the same `!fresh_write` gate and by key name (a renamed key legitimately loses it — see risks).
4. # #2607 yq: M2 streaming path still emits a raw (non-escape-sequence) U+2028/U+2029 byte unescaped in JSON output

## Background

#1982 fixed `succinctly yq`'s DOM output path (`-P`, `--arg`, `-r`/`-j`/`-0`,
`--eval-all`, `--split-exp`, and other materializing routes) to escape
U+2028/U+2029 (line/paragraph separator) in JSON output, matching real yq
(confirmed live against v4.53.3: it escapes both unconditionally, regardless
of source).

## Remaining bug

The M2 streaming path (used by a plain identity query, `.`, and most simple
navigation filters) still emits both separators raw when they arrive as an
actual UTF-8 byte already present in the source -- as opposed to a YAML
`\L`/`\P` escape sequence, which the streaming transcoder
(`stream_transcode_double_quoted_to_json` in `src/yaml/light.rs`) already
special-cases correctly.

Confirmed reproducible against real yq v4.53.3, using a JSON input file with
a literal UTF-8 U+2028/U+2029 byte in a string value (not a YAML `\L`/`\P`
escape -- JSON input is a syntactic subset of YAML flow, per #996, so it goes
through the same YAML parser/streaming writer):

```console
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y\xe2\x80\xa9z"}' | succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.'
{"a":"xy z"}          # <- WRONG: raw separator bytes, unescaped
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y\xe2\x80\xa9z"}' | yq -o json -I0 '.'
{"a":"x\u2028y\u2029z"}
```

## Root cause (hypothesis)

Same shape as #2591 (a zero-copy fast path that echoes a source span
verbatim when it contains no backslash-escape, without checking for a
different kind of "needs escaping on output" condition). The streaming
transcoder's own fast path presumably only special-cases the *decoded*
`\L`/`\P` two-character escape sequence as it's being transcoded
character-by-character, but has a separate byte-span-copying fast path for
runs with no backslash at all -- which a raw U+2028/U+2029 byte would take,
since it's not preceded by a backslash in the source. Not yet located
precisely; needs the same kind of investigation #1982's own fix required
(tracing which conversion/transcoding function the plain identity route
actually calls).

## Suggested fix direction

Likely the same shape as #1982's DOM-path fix (`write_json_body_yq`'s new
`write_yq_span_escaping_separators` helper, gated on a cheap `contains(0xE2)`
byte-existence probe before doing a per-character walk) -- but applied to
whichever streaming-transcoder fast path is responsible for copying an
unescaped span of double-quoted-scalar content verbatim.


---

## Comments on this issue


**Comment by newhoggy:**

## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** still reproduces, and the leak is wider than "the no-backslash span fast path" -- it is every raw-separator spelling on the streaming route, plus the YAML `\u2028`/`\U00002029` escapes. Verified with `od -c` against yq v4.53.3:

```console
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y\xe2\x80\xa9z"}' | succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.'   # {"a":"x<E2 80 A8>y<E2 80 A9>z"}  raw
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y\xe2\x80\xa9z"}' | yq -o json -I0 '.'              # {"a":"x\u2028y\u2029z"}
$ printf 'a: "x\\ty\xe2\x80\xa8z"\n' | succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.'   # {"a":"x\ty<raw>z"}   (backslash present -> slow transcoder path, still raw)
$ printf 'a: "x\\u2028y"\n'          | succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.'   # {"a":"x<raw>y"}      (YAML \u escape; yq: "x\u2028y")
$ printf 'a: "x\\U00002029y"\n'      | succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.'   # raw                  (yq: "x\u2029y")
$ printf "a: 'x\xe2\x80\xa8y'\n"     | succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.'   # raw                  (yq: "x\u2028y")
$ printf 'a: "x\\Ly"\n'              | succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.'   # {"a":"x\u2028y"}     (already correct, the \L/\P arm)
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y"}'   | succinctly yq -o json -I0 'to_entries'      # \u2028   (DOM route, #1982, correct)
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y"}'   | succinctly yq -o json -I0 --arg q 1 '.'     # \u2028   (DOM route, correct)
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y"}'   | succinctly yq -o json -I0 -P '.'            # raw  -- -P does not force DOM at -I0 (#2606's second bug), so this streams
$ printf '{"a": "x\xe2\x80\xa8y"}'   | succinctly jq -c '.'   # raw; /usr/bin/jq 1.7.1 also raw  -> jq mode must NOT change
```

Two neighbouring divergences surfaced while probing, out of scope here but worth their own issue: (1) in *YAML* output real yq re-escapes a raw separator inside a double-quoted scalar as `\L`/`\P` (`a: "x<raw>y"` -> `a: "x\Ly"`) on both routes, succinctly emits the raw byte on both; (2) go-yaml treats a raw U+2028 as a line break, so real yq rejects it in a plain scalar or a key (`a: x<raw>y` -> `could not find expected ':'`, `"x<raw>y": 1` -> `mapping values are not allowed`) while succinctly accepts both.

**Root cause / mechanism:** three writers in `src/yaml/light.rs` copy content without looking for the two separators, and every streaming string spelling ends in one of them:
1. `stream_json_string` -- "the single string writer for both sinks" of the YAML->JSON streaming path. It copies `&s[i..escape_pos]` between stops of `find_json_escape` (`src/util/simd/escape.rs`), which halts only on `"`, `\` and `< 0x20`. Reached by the double-quoted no-backslash fast path and the single-quoted fast path in `stream_yaml_string_to_json`, by block scalars, by plain scalars via `ResolvedScalar::Str`, and by every key writer (`stream_json_string(out, &key_str)`).
2. `stream_transcode_double_quoted_to_json` (and its single-quoted twin `stream_transcode_single_quoted_to_json`) -- the `_ =>` default arm copies a `from_utf8` chunk verbatim; only the literal `\L`/`\P` escape arm writes `\u2028`/`\u2029`.
3. `stream_json_escape` -- `c => out.write_char(c)` for everything `>= 0x20` (#532's "raw for everything else" policy), which is where `\u2028`/`\U00002028` YAML escapes land after decoding.
The DOM path is already right because `write_json_body_yq` (`src/jq/escape.rs`) routes spans through `write_yq_span_escaping_separators` (#1982); the streaming writer deliberately does not delegate to it (a measured 14% x86_64 cost to jq callers from the `#[inline]` it needs -- see the `stream_json_string` doc comment and #965), so the fix has to be replicated locally.

**Plan:**
1. `stream_json_string` (`yaml/light.rs`): after `find_json_escape` returns a span, write it through a separator-aware copy -- either make `jq::escape::write_yq_span_escaping_separators` `pub(crate)` and call it (it is `#[inline]` and already has the `contains(&0xE2)` memchr gate, so a span without `0xE2` costs one probe), or add a yq-only stop byte `0xE2` to a `find_json_escape_yq` variant of the SIMD scanner and handle `E2 80 A8`/`E2 80 A9` inline at the stop (one pass instead of two; then the writer must emit the full 3-byte char for any other `0xE2`-led code point, never a lone byte). Prefer the first for a minimal diff unless the A/B in step 5 says otherwise.
2. `stream_json_escape`: add `'\u{2028}' => "\\u2028"`, `'\u{2029}' => "\\u2029"` arms above the `c => write_char(c)` fallback, with a comment that this is the one exception to #532's raw-above-0x20 policy (yq escapes these two unconditionally -- `jq::escape` already documents the table as "five differences").
3. `stream_transcode_double_quoted_to_json` / `stream_transcode_single_quoted_to_json`: route the default-arm chunk copy through the same separator-aware writer as step 1.
4. Do **not** touch `find_json_escape` itself, `src/jq/stream.rs::stream_json_string` or `write_json_body` -- jq mode's raw output matches jq 1.7.1 and is a mode rule (ADR-0018 rule 2).
5. Perf: this is P9's hot path (`stream_json_string` is `#[inline]`-sensitive to ~1%). Run the interleaved A/B (`docs/guides/benchmarking.md`) on ARM and x86_64 with `dev bench yq` identity/`-o json` at >= 1 MB on a strings-heavy generator pattern; the `0xE2` memchr per span is expected neutral, but pin it. If step 1's two-pass form regresses, take the single-pass scanner variant.
6. Tests: `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs` streaming-route captures for every spelling above (JSON input raw, YAML double-quoted raw, single-quoted raw, backslash+raw slow path, `\u2028`, `\U00002029`, block scalar, key position from JSON input, and `.a` navigation), asserting the `\u2028`/`\u2029` bytes; keep `test_line_paragraph_separators_escaped_through_dom_path_1982` as the DOM control and add a jq-mode must-not-change assertion (raw). Unit tests next to `stream_json_string` for a span with an unrelated `0xE2`-led char (em dash U+2014, bullet U+2022) proving the probe never mis-escapes. A `-C` colored and an `--ascii-output` case (the `AsciiEscapeWriter` sink already escapes non-ASCII; confirm it still yields `\u2028`, not double-escaping).
7. Docs: `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` -- the #1693/#1700 paragraph says the streaming route "recovers" `\L`/`\P` escaping; qualify it to say raw separators were still leaking until this fix; file the two YAML-side divergences above as a new issue and cross-link.

**Risks / open questions:**
- Hot-path regression risk is the only real one; the change is otherwise mechanical. The single-pass scanner option changes SIMD code shared by the yq streamer only if a separate `_yq` entry is added -- keep jq's scanner untouched.
- `-P -I0` streaming instead of DOM (#2606) means `-P` is not a valid "force DOM" control in tests; use `to_entries`/`--arg`.

**Dependencies / related:** #1982 (DOM fix and helper), #965 (why the writer is a separate copy), #532 (raw-above-0x20 policy this narrows), #1700 (`AsciiEscapeWriter`), #2606 (`-I0 -P` routing). No open PR references #2607.

**Class:** Opus -- three writer sites on the P9 streaming hot path (one of them the shared `stream_json_escape` whose #532 policy must be narrowed by exactly two code points), a shared-scanner boundary with jq mode that must not move, and a mandatory interleaved two-architecture A/B before merging. The code diff is small, but the performance verification and the mode boundary are where the judgment is.

# #2643 yq: `del()`/writes through a `$var` bound from a navigated position diverge from yq's node semantics **Severity: Low** (refuse-only — exit 1, no document written) ## Summary Real yq's variables carry **node identity** (the Go `*yaml.Node`), so a write or `del()` through a `$var` bound from a navigated position acts on *that node* regardless of where the pipe currently is — or no-ops. succinctly's shared path resolver raises jq's "Invalid path expression" instead. Found while planning #2042 (2026-09-08); recorded here because `substitute_bound_var` is shared by both evaluators, so #2042's jq-mode widening has to be gated on `EvalTag::Jq` and this needs its own oracle matrix. ## Repro (`main` @ baa26d72e vs yq v4.53.3), input `a: {b: 1}` / `c: {b: 1}` | filter | yq v4.53.3 | succinctly yq | |-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `(.a as $y \| .a \| $y.b) = 5` | no-op, document unchanged, exit 0 | `Error: Invalid path expression near attempt to access element "b" of {"b":1}`, exit 1 | | `(.a as $y \| .c \| $y.b) = 5` | no-op, exit 0 | same error, exit 1 | | `del(.a as $y \| .c \| $y)` | deletes **`.a`** (the bound node); output `c: {b: 1}` | `Error: Invalid path expression with result {"b":1}`, exit 1 | Rows that already agree (no-op in both): `(.a as $y | .c | $y) = 5`, `(.a as $y | .a | $y) = 5`, `(. as $x | .c | $x) = 5`. ```console $ printf 'a:\n b: 1\nc:\n b: 1\n' | yq 'del(.a as $y | .c | $y)' c: b: 1 $ printf 'a:\n b: 1\nc:\n b: 1\n' | succinctly yq 'del(.a as $y | .c | $y)' Error: Invalid path expression with result {"b":1} ``` ## Notes - The `del()` row is not jq's register model at all: yq deletes the node `$y` was bound to, and the intervening `.c` is irrelevant. Matching it needs a yq-mode rule on `EvalSemantics`, not a wider jq gate (ADR-0018: the mode decides). - The two `= 5` rows are silent no-ops in yq — whether that is designed or a yq bug, it is the reference behaviour (rule 3), and a no-op is not one of the divergence conditions. - Needs a live matrix first (`=`, `|=`, `+=`, `del`, through `$y`, `$y.b`, `$y[0]`, with the bound node at `.`, a sibling, and a descendant), the same discipline #1351 used for alias writes. ## Related - #2042 — jq-mode gate widening; must not reach yq mode. - #1351 — yq write-through-alias, the closest existing yq node-identity model. --- ## Comments on this issue **Comment by newhoggy:** Found the same class again while probing #2072's own step-5 follow-ups (2026-09-08), with a simpler direct repro than the sibling-navigated rows above — writing straight through `$x` right after the bind, no intervening `.c`/`.a` hop: ```console $ printf 'a:\n - 1\n - 2\n - 3\n' > arr.yaml $ yq '.a as $x | $x[0] = 9' arr.yaml a: - 1 - 2 - 3 $ succinctly yq '.a as $x | $x[0] = 9' arr.yaml Error: Invalid path expression near attempt to access element 0 of [1,2,3] $ yq '.a as $x | del($x[0])' arr.yaml a: - 1 - 2 - 3 $ succinctly yq '.a as $x | del($x[0])' arr.yaml Error: Invalid path expression near attempt to access element 0 of [1,2,3] $ yq '.a as $x | $x[0] |= 9 | $x' arr.yaml - 9 - 2 - 3 $ succinctly yq '.a as $x | $x[0] |= 9 | $x' arr.yaml Error: Invalid path expression near attempt to access element 0 of [1,2,3] ``` `-i` on a scratch copy confirms the refusal leaves the file byte-identical in all three cases, matching this issue's own refuse-only framing (exit 1, nothing written). This exact matrix cell (`$y[0]` right at the bind site, not through a sibling) is already named in this issue's own "Needs a live matrix first" note as one of the still-open cells, and is now pinned in the codebase by `test_write_through_bound_variable_stays_refused_2072` (`tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`) as of #2072's own step-0 capture. Adding here rather than filing separately — same root cause and same refuse-only direction as the sibling-navigated rows already on this issue. **Comment by newhoggy:** ## Triage plan (2026-09-12) **Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** still reproduces, and the matrix is now captured. All three body rows plus the 2026-09-08 comment's `$x[0]` rows refuse with `Invalid path expression …`, exit 1. Re-probed live against Homebrew yq v4.53.3 on `a: {b: 1}` / `c: {b: 1}` (`-o json -I0`): | filter | yq v4.53.3 | succinctly yq | |----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------| | `.a as $y \| $y.b = 5` | doc unchanged | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| $y.b = 5 \| $y` | `{"b":5}` | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| $y.b = .c.b + 10 \| $y` | `{"b":11}` (rhs against `.`) | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| $y.b \|= . + 100 \| $y` | `{"b":101}` | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| $y.b += .c.b \| $y` | `{"b":2}` | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| del($y.b) \| $y` | `{}` | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| $y = 5 \| $y` | `5` | **`{"b":1}`, exit 0** (silently wrong) | | `.a as $y \| del($y)` | `{"c":{"b":1}}` | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| del($y) \| $y` | `{"b":1}` (`$y` survives) | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a.b as $y \| del($y)` | `{"a":{},"c":{"b":1}}` | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a.b as $y \| .a \| del($y)` | `{}` | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| .c \| del($y)` | `{"b":1}` (output is `.c`) | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a as $y \| del($y) \| .a = 3 \| del($y)` | `{"c":{"b":1}}` (deleted again) | refuses, exit 1 | | `.a[1] as $y \| del(.a[0]) \| del($y)` | `{"a":[2]}` (stale index, live parent) | refuses, exit 1 | | `. as $y \| del($y)` | doc unchanged | **empty output, exit 0** | | `. as $y \| del($y.a)` | doc unchanged | **deletes `.a`, exit 0** | | `. as $y \| $y.a.b = 5` | doc unchanged | **writes `.a.b`, exit 0** | | `(.a as $y \| .c \| $y.b) = 5` | doc unchanged | refuses, exit 1 | | `(.a as $y \| $y) = 5` | doc unchanged | doc unchanged (agrees) | | `{"x":1} as $y \| del($y)` | doc unchanged | (constructed source; no origin) | So the class is wider than "refuse-only": the four bold rows are *accepting* divergences on `main` today (`. as $y` gets `Origin::Snapshot` from `is_identity_passthrough`, so the write goes to the document where yq writes a copy; `$y = 5` is silently ignored). **Root cause / mechanism:** verified from the yq v4.53.3 source, not guessed: - `variableLoopSingleChild` (`pkg/yqlib/operator_variables.go`) stores `candidate.Copy()` for `as` (only `ref $x` stores the node itself). `Copy()` (`candidate_node.go`) keeps the original's `Parent`/`Key` but re-parents the copied *children* onto the copy. So: a write through `$y` (`$y.b = 5`, `$y = 5`, `|=`, `+=`, `del($y.b)`) mutates the **copy** — the document is untouched, but every later read of `$y` in that body sees the mutated value; the assignment stage itself evaluates to its input (`.`). - `deleteChildOperator` (`operator_delete.go`) deletes by `candidate.Parent` + the last component of `candidate.GetPath()`. For a bare `$y` that parent is the **original, live** parent node, so `del($y)` removes the bound node's key/index from the document — positionally (the stale index row and the "deleted again after `.a = 3`" row prove it is key/index-from-live-parent, not node identity). `del($y.b)` hits the copy (its parent is the copy). A root-bound `$y` has no parent, so `del($y)` is a no-op; a constructed source has none either. - succinctly: `resolve_bind_source` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) is gated `S::TAG != EvalTag::Jq → by_value()`, so a yq-mode binding is a plain `substitute_var` literal; `resolve_leaf` on `{"b":1} | .b` then raises the jq-style refusal. The `. as $y` rows go through `substitute_bound_var_at`'s `Origin::Snapshot` branch and `resolve_node`'s `Expr::TrackedVar` arm, which certifies by value equality and hands the write the real path. **Plan:** 1. Add a yq-mode rewrite `rewrite_yq_var_write_stages(body, var) -> Expr` (next to `rewrite_yq_del_comma_branches` in `src/jq/eval.rs`), applied to the `as` body before substitution in **both** evaluators — `eval_as` (`eval.rs`) and `each_as_generic`/`eval_owned_identity_as` (`eval_generic.rs`) — gated on `S::TAG == EvalTag::Yq`. Walk the body's `Expr::Pipe` stages (through `Expr::Paren`); at the first stage whose target is var-rooted (`Expr::Assign`/`Update`/`CompoundAssign`/`AlternativeAssign` with `path` headed by `Expr::Var(var)`, or `Builtin::Del(p)` with `p` headed by `Expr::Var(var)` **and at least one navigation step after it**), rewrite `stages[i..]` to the copy semantics via a rebind: - `$y

|= f | rest` → `($y |

|= f) as $y | rest` - `$y

= rhs | rest` and the `op=` forms → `rhs as $__rhs_N | ($y |

= $__rhs_N) as $y | rest` (rhs is evaluated against the stage input `.`, not `$y` — the `.c.b + 10` row pins that; `|=` needs no pre-bind). - `del($y

) | rest` → `($y | del(

)) as $y | rest`. - empty `rest` → body `.`, so the stage still evaluates to its input. The rebind is an ordinary `Expr::As`, so the existing literal substitution machinery carries the mutated copy to every later `$y` with no environment threading; `substitute_var_impl`'s shadowing arm keeps the outer binding out of the new body. 2. Bare `del($y)` (no navigation after the var) in yq mode: bind with a marker. Lift `resolve_bind_source`'s jq gate to `S::TAG == EvalTag::Jq || S::TAG == EvalTag::Yq` for the *witness* only (the `Origin::At` marker from `resolve_bind_source_in`), and make `eval_as`/`each_as_generic` pass the origin through `substitute_bound_var_from` the way #2072 does. Then add a `purpose: ResolvePurpose::{Path, Assign, Delete}` field to `Frame` (set in `Frame::enter` by the three entry points: `builtin_del`/`builtin_delpaths`, the assignment entry, and `path()`), and in `resolve_node`'s `Expr::TrackedVar` arm add a yq-only branch ahead of the `frame.certifies` check: for `Origin::At { invocation, path }` with `invocation == frame.invocation` and `purpose == Delete`, if `frame.at` is a proper-or-equal prefix of `path`, yield the branch `path` minus that prefix (relative to the current stage input — this is what makes `.a.b as $y | .a | del($y)` delete `.b` and `.a as $y | del($y)` delete `.a`); if `frame.at` is not a prefix (the `.c | del($y)` row) or `path` is `Root` (`. as $y | del($y)`), yield **no branch** — a no-op, output unchanged. `purpose == Assign` with any var-rooted target yields no branch too (the `(.a as $y | .c | $y.b) = 5` and `(.a as $y | $y) = 5` rows), replacing today's refusal and the `. as $y | $y.a.b = 5` acceptance. Keep `purpose == Path` on the existing jq rule so `path($y)` is untouched. 3. `Origin::Snapshot` in yq mode: `substitute_bound_var_at` must stop granting `Snapshot` for an identity source when `S::TAG == Yq` — step 1's rewrite already intercepts `. as $y | $y.a.b = 5` and `del($y.a)` when they are pipe stages, but the nested-in-LHS shape (`(. as $y | $y.a) = 5`) must fall to step 2's no-branch rule, not the value-equality certification. Probed: `yq '(. as $y | $y.a) = 5'` leaves the doc unchanged; succinctly writes `{"a":5,...}` today — a fifth accepting divergence, same fix. 4. Both evaluators: the `alias_identity` mirror (#1351) runs after `builtin_del`; a `del($y)` resolved to a real path goes through the same `delete_at_path` route, so nothing new is needed there, but add one anchor-bearing case to the tests to prove it. 5. Tests: extend `test_write_through_bound_variable_stays_refused_2072` (`tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`) into an accepting matrix — every row of the table above, both `-o json` and YAML output, plus `-i` on a scratch copy for the `del($y)` and `$y.b = 5 | $y` rows (yq's `-i` writes the *pipeline output*, so `.a as $y | .c | del($y)` writes `b: 1` to the file — pin that exactly). Add a jq-mode guard row (`/usr/bin/jq` 1.7.1: `.a as $y | $y.b = 5` and `.a as $y | del($y)` both raise `Invalid path expression …`, exit 5 — verified) in `tests/cli_tests.rs`. Unit tests for the rewrite in `src/jq/eval.rs` (`rest` empty, nested `Paren`, shadowed re-bind `.a as $y | $y.b = 5 | .a as $y | $y` → `{"b":1}`, generator rhs `$y.b = (1,2) | $y` → yq gives one output `{"b":2}`, so the pre-bind must take the *last* value, not fan out — probe again when implementing). 6. Docs: `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` — record what stays divergent: (a) `.[] as $y | del($y)` prints `{}` twice in yq (both results are the one mutated root) where succinctly prints two per-binding copies; (b) `.c | del($y) | parent` shows the live root with `.a` gone in yq, unreachable in succinctly's value model; (c) `($y.b = 5), $y` comma-shape mutation is not carried (yq itself prints a single line there — capture before documenting). Add a `ref $x` note: real yq's by-reference binding is unparsed in succinctly (`parse error at position 3: unexpected character 'r'`) and is a separate feature, not this issue. Update the #2643 sentence in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md` and the `sub`/anchor sections' neighbour in `CLAUDE.md` (a short "writes through `as`-bound variables" paragraph next to the #1351 one). **Risks / open questions:** - The rewrite changes shapes that *currently work by accident* (`. as $y | $y.a.b = 5` writing the document). That is the correct direction per the reference, but it is a behaviour change for anyone relying on it — call it out in the PR. - `Frame` gains a field read by one arm; every `Frame::enter` caller must set it — an omission defaults to `Path` and merely keeps today's refusal, so the failure mode is safe. - The rebind rewrite runs before substitution, so it must not fire when `var` is shadowed between the bind and the stage (`substitute_var_impl`'s shadow logic is the model to copy). - `$__rhs_N` must be a name the parser cannot produce so it can never collide with a user variable. - `ref $x` should get its own issue (I have not filed one — flagging here). **Dependencies / related:** #2042 (jq-mode witness this reuses — its gate must stay jq-only for `path()`), #2072 (origin-carrying `substitute_bound_var_from`), #1351 (alias write model, same "copy model recovering node identity" shape). No open PR references #2643. **Class:** Opus — the fix touches both evaluators' `as` sites, adds a purpose flag through `Frame` and a yq-only branch in the shared `resolve_node` walker, and the semantics had to be re-derived from a 20-row oracle matrix plus the yq source (copy-on-bind versus delete-via-live-parent are two different mechanisms that a single "node identity" rule would get wrong). No new representation or ADR is needed — the origin markers, `Frame::at` and the `as`-rebind substitution already exist — so it is not Fable; but the accepting-direction rows and the mode gating carry real regression risk across the write family, so not Sonnet. **Comment by newhoggy:** More rows in this class, found while working #3207 (`main` @ ff7059a3a vs yq v4.53.3). These are **silent discards**, not refusals: succinctly prints nothing and exits 0, while yq prints the document unchanged. | input | filter | yq v4.53.3 | succinctly yq | |----------|------------------------|--------------------|-------------------------| | `a: 1` | `del(. as $x \| $x)` | `a: 1`, exit 0 | *(no output)*, exit 0 | | `null` | `del(. as $x \| $x)` | `null`, exit 0 | *(no output)*, exit 0 | | `true` | `del(. as $x \| $x)` | `true`, exit 0 | *(no output)*, exit 0 | | `null` | `. as $x \| del($x)` | `null`, exit 0 | *(no output)*, exit 0 | The `$x` bound at the root resolves to the root path `[]`. `resolve_del_path_branches` turns that into `DelPaths::Root`, and yq's bare-`del(.)` rule (#1702) then prints nothing. This is the same mechanism #3207 fixed for a literal `del(null)`. It doesn't go through #3125's terminal carve-out, though: the root-bound `$x` is certified by the register/frame, so #3207's fix doesn't reach it. That makes it worse than the refuse-only severity above. The navigated-bind rows still refuse, as this issue already records: `del(.a as $x | $x)` on `a: 1\nb: 2` gives yq `b: 2`, succinctly `Invalid path expression with result 1`. **Comment by newhoggy:** More rows found while working #3207. All of them behave the same on `main` @ ff7059a3a and on the #3207 branch, so they predate it. | input | filter | yq v4.53.3 | succinctly yq | |-----------------------|---------------------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------| | `a: null` / `b: null` | `.a as $y \| .b \|= del($y)` | `b: null` (`.a` deleted) | document unchanged, exit 0 (**silent**) | | `a: true` / `b: true` | `.a as $y \| .b \|= del($y)` | `b: true` (`.a` deleted) | document unchanged, exit 0 (**silent**) | | `a: {b: 1}` | `del(.a \| tojson)` | `{}` (`.a` deleted) | `Invalid path expression with result "{\"b\":1}"`, exit 1 | The `tojson` row shows yq's own path propagation reaching past scalar-producing builtins: `tojson` keeps its input's path. #3207 depends on this. succinctly's "untracked" is wider than yq's "has no path", so #3207 only lets `del()` skip a `null`/`true`/`false` literal identical to its input. Every other untracked target keeps refusing, which is why `del(1)` still refuses even though yq no-ops it. If this issue gives succinctly yq-style node identity, that restriction can be revisited.

# #2663 jq/yq: the yq JSON-escape fork rests on a one-architecture number and a fn-pointer call

**Severity: Low** (perf / verification; split out of #965 item 12)

## Summary

`src/jq/stream.rs` and `src/yaml/light.rs` each carry their own copy of yq's JSON string
escape loop over the same `find_json_escape` SIMD scan. PR #1638 kept them as a deliberate
fork because the two callers appeared to want opposite inlining: adding `#[inline]` to the
shared `jq::escape::write_json_body_yq` cost jq's `arrays keys_unsorted` **+13.9% on a
7950X**, while `light.rs`'s streaming YAML->JSON path reads ~+1% across the yq corpus
*without* the body inlined. The rationale is recorded in `light.rs`'s `stream_json_string`
doc comment and in `docs/parsing/yaml.md`.

Two gaps in that finding, both verifiable now:

1. **Only the x86_64 number exists.** No ARM figure was ever recorded for the jq side, so
   there is no evidence the two callers need opposite inlining on both platforms
   (CLAUDE.md: memory-bound effects do not port across architectures; name both chips).
2. **The jq caller reaches the escaper through a bare `fn` pointer**, which already blocks
   cross-function inlining at that boundary regardless of any attribute on the callee.
   Verified on current `main`: every `escape` parameter in `src/jq/stream.rs` is declared
   `escape: fn(&mut W, &str) -> core::fmt::Result` (four sites, `:473`, `:505`, `:655`,
   `:694`), and `stream_owned_value_json` passes `write_json_body_yq` as a value through
   `stream_owned_value_json_with`; `stream_lazy_keys_json` calls
   `stream_json_string(out, &key, write_json_body_yq)` the same way. The 14% may be an
   artefact of an inlining change interacting with a fn-pointer call, not evidence that the
   two bodies cannot share one definition.

## Proposed work

- Replace the `fn` pointer parameters in `stream.rs` with a generic closure bound
  (`F: Fn(&mut W, &str) -> core::fmt::Result`) so each call site monomorphizes and LLVM
  can inline the escaper at its discretion.
- Re-run #1638's three-way comparison (fork as-is / shared `write_json_body_yq` without
  attribute / shared with `#[inline]`) with `scripts/ab-cli.py`, interleaved, both modes,
  on **both** pinned machines, against a baseline binary built from the merge-base rather
  than an earlier commit of the same branch.
- Decide from the numbers: if the `arrays keys_unsorted` penalty disappears once the
  indirection is gone, collapse `light.rs`'s copy onto `jq::escape::write_json_body_yq`
  and delete the fork's rationale; if it survives on either chip, record the ARM figure
  next to the x86_64 one and keep the fork with the stronger justification.

Per CLAUDE.md's attribution rule, the fn-pointer removal must be measured **on its own**
first (no other change in the binary), so the 14% can be charged to inlining or to the
indirection and not to both at once.

## Why not just do it in #965

#965 is a Tier 3 tracker mixing design questions with mechanical work; this item has no
design question, only a measurement gate, and both bench machines are reachable today. Do
not put a closing keyword against #965 in the PR body.


---

## Comments on this issue


**Comment by newhoggy:**

## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** still holds, and the fork has since grown a *behavioural* difference on top of the perf question. Both claims re-verified by reading the code: every `escape` parameter in `src/jq/stream.rs` (`stream_owned_value_json_with`, `stream_owned_value_json_with_at_depth`, `write_object_entries`, `stream_json_string`) is still a bare `fn(&mut W, &str) -> core::fmt::Result`, and `stream_owned_value_json` still passes `write_json_body_yq` by value; `src/yaml/light.rs::stream_json_string` is still `#[inline]` and still carries the "deliberately not delegating" rationale, mirrored in `docs/parsing/yaml.md` (O3 "Where this code lives now"). No ARM figure has been added anywhere.

The new part: #1982 (`1e29300a8`) taught `jq::escape::write_json_body_yq` to escape U+2028/U+2029 via `write_yq_span_escaping_separators`, and — exactly because of this fork — `light.rs::stream_json_string` never got it. Live, with a raw U+2028 byte in a quoted scalar:

```
$ printf 'a: "x\xe2\x80\xa8y"\nb: [1]\n' > sep.yaml
$ succinctly yq -o json -I0 '.' sep.yaml | od -c           # x  \xe2\x80\xa8  y   <- raw, streaming path (light.rs copy)
$ succinctly yq -o json -I0 --arg x 1 '.' sep.yaml | od -c # x  \  u  2  0  2  8  y  <- escaped, DOM path (write_json_body_yq)
$ yq -o json -I0 '.' sep.yaml | od -c                      # x  \  u  2  0  2  8  y  <- real yq v4.53.3
```

That residual is already tracked as #2607 (open, Opus/Triaged). So the fork is not only unmeasured on ARM — it has already done the thing duplicated escapers do (CLAUDE.md's #106 lesson), and #2607's fix would otherwise add a *second* copy of `write_yq_span_escaping_separators`. No open PR references #2663.

**Root cause / mechanism:** `stream.rs` threads the escaper as a `fn` pointer through four recursive parameters so one `stream_owned_value_json_with` serves both `write_json_body_jq` and `write_json_body_yq`. A call through a `fn` pointer is an indirect call unless LLVM can prove the pointee at the call site; with the pointer passed down a recursive function it usually cannot, so an attribute on the callee changes the callee's own codegen (and its layout in the binary) without ever enabling inlining at the jq call sites — which is why the +13.9% in #1638 could not distinguish "inlining hurt" from "code layout/CGU partitioning moved" (the class #2603 later pinned with `codegen-units=1` + fat LTO; that pin post-dates #1638's measurement, so the 14% was taken under the default 16-CGU profile that CLAUDE.md now records as producing ±5% on x86 identity queries from partitioning alone).

**Plan (measurement gated; do not run benchmarks concurrently with anything else on either box):**
1. **Build the baseline once**: a release binary from the merge-base of the feature branch with `main` (not from an earlier commit of the same branch — `feedback_ab_baseline_must_predate_your_own_first_commit`), on each of the two pinned machines (M4 Pro `johns-mac-mini`, 7950X `terminus`), both with the current `[profile.release]` pin so profile is not a variable. Run `scripts/ab-cli.py --before <base> --control --corpus <dir>` on each machine first and keep the control row as the noise floor.
2. **Corpus**: ≥ 1 MB inputs only (rule 2). Generate with `succinctly json generate` / `dsv generate` and the `yq` suite patterns: one JSON `arrays`-shaped file (the `arrays keys_unsorted` row from #1638), one wide-object JSON file (the shape where the escaper is called most per byte — many short keys), one `strings`/`long_strings` YAML file (long quoted scalars, few escapes), one block-scalar YAML file (the O3 shape), and one file with escapes every ~20 chars. The escaper is charged per string; the wide-object and short-key shapes are where a call-overhead change shows, the long-string ones are where it cannot help (CLAUDE.md: measure a precheck where the guarded code is already fastest).
3. **Step A — indirection removal, alone** (`src/jq/stream.rs`): change the four `escape: fn(&mut W, &str) -> Result` parameters to a generic `F: Fn(&mut W, &str) -> core::fmt::Result` (pass by `&F` or `impl Fn` through the recursion; `write_object_entries` and `stream_json_string` take the same bound). No other change in the binary. A/B against the baseline on both machines: `--tool jq --queries 'keys_unsorted' '.' '.[]' 'to_entries'` on the JSON corpus and `--tool yq --queries '.' '.[]'` on the YAML corpus, both `-o json -I0`, `--reps 9`. Expected: neutral or small win; a change here alone is attributable purely to the indirect call.

# #2664 jq/yaml: fold the two hand-maintained cursor-to-OwnedValue walks onto their generic twins

**Severity: Low** (maintenance; split out of #965 items 3 and 8)

## Summary

Two hand-maintained materializer pairs remain after #907, #1247 and #2636, each a full
recursive document-to-`OwnedValue` walk kept in sync by hand with its generic twin. One
design question, two symptoms.

## A. `lazy.rs::cursor_to_owned` / `cursor_to_owned_at_depth` vs `eval_generic::to_owned_cursor` / `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` (item 8)

`src/jq/lazy.rs` hand-writes a JSON-only tree walk (`cursor_to_owned_at_depth`, ~100
lines on current `main`) even though `JsonCursor` already implements the `DocumentCursor`
trait the generic `to_owned_cursor` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`, ~100 lines) is written
against. Every cross-cutting fix has had to land twice: #998's nesting guard was added to
the generic walk first and the `lazy.rs` copy was only found once `-e` raw-overflowed the
stack; #1247's decode-error routing and the undecodable-key wording were applied to both by
hand. This is the JSON-specific instance of the shape below.

## B. `yq_runner.rs::yaml_to_owned_value` vs `eval.rs::yaml_value_to_owned_checked` (item 3)

Both take a `YamlCursor`, do the explicit-tag lookup, the quoted-string short-circuit and
the recursive sequence/mapping walk, and share only the innermost `ResolvedScalar` match
(#907). They have since diverged on purpose in one place: the `yq_runner.rs` copy
materializes through `to_owned_value_for_json_bridge` because its output is headed for the
`to_json_for_reindex` round trip that would otherwise flatten a tag-forced `!!float 2`
(#1176), and the `eval.rs` copy drives `DisplayKeyGuard` by hand because it does not go
through `DocumentFields`/`resolve_display_key` (#1801).

## What is not settled

The earlier review of the `StandardJson` pair found that "near-identical" copies in this
family carry real behavioural differences (NaN-sentinel decoding, malformed-UTF-8 fallback),
so the first step is a **behavioural diff**, not a delegate. For A: enumerate what
`cursor_to_owned_at_depth` does that `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` does not (and vice versa),
with a test per difference, before folding. For B: decide whether the `for_json_bridge`
variant is a parameter of one walk or a reason to keep two. A is the better entry point:
JSON-only, both sides already share the fallible `Result<OwnedValue, EvalError>` shape from
#1247, and success there shows the pattern for B.

# #2705 yq: a metadata assignment nested under `as` (`.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x`) is refused; real yq applies it

## Summary

A yq metadata assignment (`line_comment =`, `style =`, `anchor =`, #798) is refused with an explicit error whenever it sits anywhere other than a top-level pipe stage. The most common shape that hits this is a variable binding feeding the right-hand side:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: hi\n' | yq '.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x'
a: 1 # hi
b: hi
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: hi\n' | succinctly yq '.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x'
Error: metadata assignment (line_comment/style/anchor = ...) is only supported as a top-level pipe stage
```

Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`. The same refusal covers a write inside a `reduce`/`foreach` body or a `def` body.

## Why it is refused today

`resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs *before* the real evaluation. It flattens the expression's top-level pipe stages, re-evaluates each earlier stage to reach the document the write sees, then evaluates `path(TARGET)` and the right-hand side against that document via `evaluate_input`. A write nested under `Expr::As` would need `$x` bound when its RHS is evaluated, and `evaluate_input` on the RHS alone has no binding. `count_meta_assigns` compares the total number of `MetaAssign` nodes with the number of top-level stages and reports the mismatch rather than letting the nested write silently no-op (the outcome #798's triage ruled out).

Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` under "Metadata assignment (`PATH <slot> = value`): what `succinctly yq` refuses or drops".

## Possible directions

- Descend `Expr::As { source, body }` in the pre-pass: evaluate `source` against the current document, then evaluate the body's writes with the binding installed (the evaluator already has a scope mechanism for `as`; the pre-pass would need to enter it, or wrap the RHS as `SOURCE as $x | RHS` and evaluate that).
- Longer term, move the write out of the pre-pass entirely: have `eval_meta_assign` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) record `(path, slot, text)` into a thread-local drained by the runner, the way `alias_identity` threads state through a write. That removes the top-level restriction for every construct at once, but needs the ambient path prefix (the spine-2416 `with_path_base` machinery) to turn a stage-relative target into a document path.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch; the explicit error was added in that review's fixes.
- `.b as $x | (.a style = "double")` has a CLI test pinning the current refusal (`nested_metadata_assignment_is_refused_explicitly` in `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`); update it deliberately when this lands.


---

## Comments on this issue


**Comment by newhoggy:**

## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (`2581b17c9`):** still reproduces. Every `as`-bound shape I tried is applied by pinned yq v4.53.3 and refused here with `metadata assignment (line_comment/style/anchor = ...) is only supported as a top-level pipe stage`:

| input | filter | yq v4.53.3 |
|---|---|---|
| `a: 1\nb: hi` | `.b as $x \| .a line_comment = $x` | `a: 1 # hi` |
| `a: 1\nb: hi\nc: yo` | `.b as $x \| .c as $y \| .a line_comment = ($x + $y)` | `a: 1 # hiyo` |
| `a: 1\nb: hi` | `.b as $x \| .a = $x \| .a line_comment = "y"` | `a: hi # y` |
| `a: 1\nb: hi` | `.b as $x \| .a line_comment \|= . + $x` | `a: 1 # 1hi` (`.` is the candidate's value) |
| `a: 1\nb: hi` | `(.b as $x \| .a line_comment = $x) \| .b line_comment = "z"` | `a: 1 # hi` / `b: hi # z` |
| `a: 1\nb: 2` | `.[] as $x \| .a line_comment = $x` | **two** documents, both `a: 1 # 2` — the forks share the node, the last write wins in each |

# #2706 yq: navigating after a write (`.a.b = "y" | .a`) drops every comment, anchor and style the write did not touch

## Summary

When a pipe writes to the document and then *navigates* into it, the result loses every piece of presentation the write did not touch: trailing comments, anchors, quoting style. Real yq keeps them.

```
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x # c\n  d: &z "q"\n' | yq '.a.b = "y" | .a'
b: y # c
d: &z "q"
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x # c\n  d: &z "q"\n' | succinctly yq '.a.b = "y" | .a'
b: y
d: q
```

The same happens after `|=` and after a #798 metadata write, which makes the metadata write itself vanish:

```
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x\n' | yq '.a.b style = "double" | .a'
b: "x"
$ printf 'a:\n  b: x\n' | succinctly yq '.a.b style = "double" | .a'
b: x
```

Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`.

## Mechanism

`evaluate_yaml_cursor` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) only builds the pristine `CommentTree` snapshot and reconciles presentation when `is_alias_sensitive_assign(expr)` holds, and that predicate's `is_shape_preserving` half returns `false` for a trailing navigation stage. So the result value is a plain `OwnedValue` with an empty tree: no comment, anchor or style survives, and the #798 write pass never runs at all (it is gated on the same `presentation_sync_ctx`).

This is not specific to #798. It is the same hole for every write form, which is why the review fix for #798 documented it under "Three known gaps this write shares with every other write form" in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` rather than erroring.

## Possible direction

Let `is_shape_preserving` admit a *trailing* static-navigation suffix (`.a`, `.a.b`, `.a[0]`) after a shape-preserving prefix, and have the reconcile step navigate the pristine tree by the same steps so the result's subtree keeps its metadata. `static_nav_steps` already exists for exactly this kind of path. A non-static trailing navigation (`.[]`, `.[(.i)]`) can stay unsupported.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch.
- Related: #1349 (a multi-result filter carries no `CommentTree` at all), which is the other route that drops all presentation.

# #2707 yq: `style = "literal"/"folded"/"tagged"` are refused and an existing block scalar is re-rendered quoted on any DOM write

## Summary

`style = "literal"`, `style = "folded"` and `style = "tagged"` are in real yq's vocabulary and all three render. succinctly parses them and refuses with an explicit "not yet supported" error, because the DOM emitter has no arm for any of them:

```
$ printf 'a: hello\n' | yq '.a style = "literal"'
a: |-
  hello
$ printf 'a: hello\n' | yq '.a style = "folded"'
a: >-
  hello
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | yq '.a style = "tagged"'
a: !!int 1
$ printf 'a: hello\n' | succinctly yq '.a style = "literal"'
Error: style = "literal" is not yet supported
```

The same emitter gap already shows on any DOM write to a document that *contains* a block scalar, with no metadata assignment involved:

```
$ printf 'a: |\n  x\n  y\n' | yq '.b = 1'
a: |
  x
  y
b: 1
$ printf 'a: |\n  x\n  y\n' | succinctly yq '.b = 1'
a: "x\ny\n"
b: 1
$ printf 'a: >\n  x\n  y\n' | succinctly yq '.b = 1'
a: "x y\n"
```

Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`.

## Mechanism

`NodeMeta.style` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) already carries `"literal"`/`"folded"` read from the cursor, but `yaml_quote_string_with_style` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) only has arms for `single`/`double` and falls back to `yaml_quote_string`, and nothing renders a tag from a style at all. `RENDERABLE_STYLES` in the same file is the allow-list the #798 write pass checks before refusing.

## What landing this needs

- Block scalar emission in `emit_yaml_value_at_depth`: `|`/`>` with the right chomping indicator (`|-` for no trailing newline, `|` for one, `|+` for more), an indentation indicator when the first line starts with a space, and the folded form's line-wrapping rules. Real yq's folded output above (`x y` followed by a blank line) is go-yaml's, so pin it from the oracle rather than the spec.
- `tagged`: the `!!int`/`!!str`/`!!bool`/`!!float`/`!!null`/`!!map`/`!!seq` tag for the value's type, and it interacts with #747 (explicit source tags are dropped on the DOM path today).
- Then drop the three names from the refusal in the #798 write pass and remove the entry from `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch.
- Related: #747 (tag preservation), #865 (style preservation).

**Comment by newhoggy:**

## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

| value | yq v4.53.3 |
|---|---|

| `"x\ny\n"` | `\|` (one → clip) |
| `"x\ny\n\n"` | `\|+` + one blank content line (two or more → keep) |
| `"\n"` | `\|+` + a blank line |
| `" lead"` | `\|2-` + `   lead` — indentation indicator when the first line starts with a space; the digit is the indent unit (`\|4-` under `-I4`) |
| `""` | `""` — go-yaml falls back to double quotes for an empty block scalar |
| `"x\ty"`, `"é\nz"`, `"- x"`, `"#x\ny"`, `"x: y\nz"` | all render as literal |
| `"hello world"` folded | `>-` + `  hello world` (no line wrapping: a 100-char line stays on one line) |

| `"x\n y"` folded | `>-` / `  x` / (blank) / `   y` — a more-indented line keeps its space |

# #2708 yq: a line_comment on a flow-sequence element re-renders the sequence in block form; real yq keeps `[1, 2, # y` + `]`

## Summary

A `line_comment` written onto an element of a *flow* sequence makes succinctly re-render the whole sequence in block form. Real yq keeps the flow form and emits the comment after a trailing comma inside the brackets:

```
$ printf 'a: [1, 2]\n' | yq '.a[1] line_comment = "y"'
a: [1, 2, # y
]
$ printf 'a: [1, 2]\n' | succinctly yq '.a[1] line_comment = "y"'
a:
  - 1
  - 2 # y
```

Same for `.a[-1]`. Both outputs read back as the same value, so this is a rendering divergence, not data loss. Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`.

## Mechanism

`is_flow_safe` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) returns `false` for a flow container whose element carries its own comment, because the flow emitter comma-joins elements on one line and has no position for a per-element comment. The container then falls back to block rendering, exactly as an *existing* element comment already does. The #798 write pass reuses that predicate deliberately so a written comment behaves like a captured one.

Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` under "Two rendering divergences" in the #798 entry.

## Open question before implementing

go-yaml's output here is peculiar (a comment after the last element's comma, then the closing bracket on its own line). Before matching it, measure a few more shapes against the oracle: a comment on a *middle* element (`.a[0] line_comment = "y"` on `[1, 2]`), a flow mapping value (`.a.b line_comment` on `a: {b: 1, c: 2}`), and a nested flow sequence, since the answer decides whether a general "flow container with commented elements" renderer is needed or just the last-element case.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch.
- Related: #794 (a flow-collection comment before the closing bracket was dropped on identity output).

# #2709 yq: stages before a metadata assignment are evaluated twice, so a side effect in an assignment RHS (`.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"`) fires twice

## Summary

When a pipe contains a #798 metadata assignment (`line_comment =`, `style =`, `anchor =`), every earlier stage is evaluated twice: once by the write pass that works out which document the metadata write sees, and once by the real evaluation. A side effect inside such a stage therefore fires twice:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",2]
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a = .a'
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2
b: 2
```

Reproduced on succinctly at `3a3e88140`. Real yq has no `debug` (its lexer rejects it), so this is only reachable through `--jq-extensions`, but the duplicated output is wrong on its own terms: the control case prints once.

## Mechanism

`resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs before evaluation. To make `.a = 2 | .b line_comment = (.a | tostring)` write `# 2` (as real yq does) it re-evaluates each stage preceding the last metadata write through `evaluate_input_quiet` and carries the first output forward as the document the next stage sees. `is_value_identity_stage` exempts a bare `debug`/`debug(msg)` *stage* precisely so its side effect isn't repeated, but a `debug` (or `stderr`, `input`, `halt_error`, ...) nested inside a stage's right-hand side is still re-run.

## Possible directions

- Detect a side-effecting builtin anywhere inside a stage that precedes a metadata write (a walk with `jq::walk::any_subexpr`, the way `count_meta_assigns` already does) and either refuse explicitly or fall back to resolving against the pristine document for that pipe.
- Or remove the re-evaluation entirely by applying the write *during* evaluation (`eval_meta_assign` recording `(path, slot, text)` into a thread-local the runner drains), which is also the route #2705 needs. That makes each stage run exactly once.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch; the pipe-sequential resolution that introduces the second evaluation was part of that review's fixes.
- `input`/`inputs` would be worse than a duplicated line (they consume input), but they are not shape-preserving so the write pass never runs for a pipe that contains them at top level; only a nested use inside an assignment RHS could reach this.


---

## Comments on this issue


**Comment by newhoggy:**

## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (`2581b17c9`):** still reproduces, and it is wider than the issue states — it is reachable *without* `--jq-extensions`, because `stderr` and `halt_error` are not gated in yq mode (real yq's lexer rejects both: `.a = (.a | stderr)` → `lexer: invalid input text "stderr)"`, same for `halt_error`; that missing gate is a separate, unfiled gap).

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",2]
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a = .a'   # control
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq '.a = (.b | stderr) | .a line_comment = "y"'      # no flag needed
22a: 2 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq '.a = (.b | halt_error) | .a line_comment = "y"'  # halts twice
2
2
[exit 1]
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a |= (. | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",1]
["DEBUG:",1]
a: 1 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = 3 | select(.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",2]
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 3 # y
b: 2
```

A `debug` inside the metadata write's *own* RHS fires once today (`.a line_comment = (.b | debug | tostring)`): only the pre-pass evaluates the RHS, the real evaluation's `eval_meta_assign` ignores it. That count must not change.

**Root cause / mechanism:** `resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs before `eval_with_cursor_using` and, to learn the document each `MetaAssign` stage sees, re-runs every preceding stage through `evaluate_input_quiet` (a fresh `JsonIndex` re-index + `jq::eval`), then the real evaluation runs the same stages again. `is_value_identity_stage` only skips a *bare* `debug`/`debug(msg)` stage; anything nested inside a stage (an assignment RHS, a `|=` filter, `select`'s predicate) runs twice, and `evaluate_input_quiet` swallows the pre-pass's own `Halt`/`Error` so a `halt_error` prints its payload twice before the real one exits.

**Plan (fix the mechanism, not the symptom — this is also the change #2705 needs, so it is done once, here):**

1. Move the write resolution *into* the real evaluation. Add a `pub mod meta_writes` to `src/jq/eval.rs` on the `alias_identity` pattern (thread-local + `enter() -> Guard` + `take()`, `#[cfg(feature = "std")]` with a no-op `no_std` stub like `yq_read_only_context`), holding `Vec<RecordedMetaWrite { path: Vec<MetaPathStep>, effect: MetaEffect }>`. Move `MetaPathStep`, `MetaEffect`, `WritableSlot`, `validate_style`, `RENDERABLE_STYLES`, `meta_comment_text`, `meta_anchor_name`, `plain_scalar_text` (or its caller), `meta_path_from_value`, `owned_value_at` from `yq_runner.rs` into that module — they are pure functions with no CLI dependency.
2. Extend the `Expr::MetaAssign` dispatch arm in `eval_single` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) to pass `value`/`is_update` into `eval_meta_assign`. In `eval_meta_assign`, *when a recorder is installed*: evaluate `path(TARGET)` against `input` (the document that stage actually sees — the runner's re-evaluation becomes unnecessary), evaluate the RHS exactly as `resolve_one_meta_assign` does today (`=`: `value | tostring` once against `input`, first output; `|=`: per candidate, `.` bound to the candidate's current value via `owned_value_at`, missing candidate reads `null`), validate (`validate_style`/`meta_anchor_name`), push the writes, then run the existing `TARGET |= .` value-tree step. Validation failures return `QueryResult::Error(..)` from here — that improves fidelity as a side effect: `.a style = "bogus" | error("boom")` reports `unknown style bogus` like yq (today succinctly reports `boom`, because the pre-pass is skipped when the pipe is not shape-preserving), and `.a style = "tagged" | .b` stops silently succeeding.
3.
